recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If BR&R wants the current primary-investigator role definition to use the older 2017 wording or a hybrid, handle that as a new review against FHIR-41330 rather than as a FHIR-14168 reconciliation fix.
issue_request: FHIR-14168 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 BR&R request to change ResearchStudy.principalInvestigator to define the principal investigator as a researcher who oversees multiple aspects of a study, including protocol work, IRB submission, recruitment, informed consent, data collection, analysis, interpretation, and presentation.
initial_application: Git commit 61b5fa557635a9d272e7508b2c7e139a895be930 explicitly included GF#14168 and changed the old ResearchStudy spreadsheet short text and definition to the requested wording. The Jira resolution states that the change was made and published in the Dec 2017 FHIR ballot.
additional_context: ResearchStudy is still active in the current build, but the standalone ResearchStudy.principalInvestigator element is no longer current source. Later Published/Persuasive FHIR-37814 deleted sponsor, principalInvestigator, and contact from ResearchStudy because their semantics are supported through associatedParty.role; source/fhir.ini maps ResearchStudy.principalInvestigator to ResearchStudy.associatedParty.party with role='primary-investigator'. Later Applied/Persuasive FHIR-41330 approved the current Research Study Party Role display and definition for primary-investigator.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. Reintroducing or restating the retired element definition would conflict with the R5 consolidation, and changing the current primary-investigator role definition back to the 2017 element wording would conflict with the later R6 role-code decision.
